review_output: {"summary":"117 fixes the 116 MINOR for stale RR/Serializable snapshots that write payments. The fix holds an SRE lock on both tables, which drains writers. It then rewrites every currently linked payment row with its existing value, so any older snapshot that later UPDATEs or DELETEs those rows gets 40001 (first updater wins). Unlinked payments are fine: a stale snapshot that still sees an old link only emits an extra event for that old window, and any later 116 link writes the payment row. The no-op touch is filtered out by the supplied source triggers because id, vendorId and metadata are unchanged. Remaining risks: lock and batch cost not measured, a possible silent row-security skip in the top-level touch, a probe that runs extracted statements rather than the migration file, narrow scenario coverage, and production side effects checked only locally. No BLOCKER found. The 7/20 gate is unchanged, so the WP is still NOT READY.","findings":[{"severity":"MAJOR","area":"upgrade lock/batch cost","file":"prisma/migrations/20261016050000_live_metric_order_upgrade_snapshot_fence/migration.sql","issue":"Unbounded table touch while holding an SRE lock on both payment and order tables","evidence":"L5 locks PaymentTransaction and CommerceOrder. L34-36 rewrite all linked payment rows in one statement. Each row queues 3 AFTER trigger events and writes a new tuple plus WAL. lock_timeout only limits waiting for the lock; there is no statement_timeout. The probe used 1 payment.","impact":"Checkout, payment webhooks and order writes are blocked for a duration that grows with the number of linked payments. Table bloat and a WAL spike are possible.
